plan: Hold all patient-facing state in the public `session` dictionary with exactly the four contracted keys, initialized from a frozen template so `begin` and `abandon` can restore it exactly.
Copy `appointments` into private id/label records at construction and keep a string-id set for O(1) validation while preserving input order for choices.

Centralize screen construction in a `_screen(prompt, messages)` builder that emits `{prompt, messages, choices}` and attaches appointment choices exactly when the prompt is `Choose appointment`, guaranteeing deterministic output.

Dispatch `handle(action)` through a type-keyed table of guard methods; each method validates preconditions and payload types fully before any mutation, returning an `Error:`-prefixed screen on failure so accepted data is never corrupted and nothing raises.
Compute post-correction prompts with a `_next_prompt` helper that walks the unmet requirements in order: unconfirmed contact, missing appointment, then review.

Inject `action_source` and `screen_sink` as constructor ports; `run_once` raises RuntimeError before touching either when one is missing, otherwise reads one action, handles it, displays the resulting screen exactly once, and returns the same screen object — making both ports trivially replaceable by standard-library unittest fakes.
mechanisms: authoritative session-state dictionary with frozen initial template
deterministic screen-builder with prompt-conditional choice attachment
type-keyed action dispatch with per-action precondition guards
validate-before-mutate error screens (Error: prefix, no state change, no exceptions)
constructor-injected input/output ports mediated by run_once
